correctness.rationale: For 0<alpha<=1, the monotonic power density gives G(x)<=alpha^(-1)x^(1-alpha)F(x^alpha). Changing variables produces the exact weighted inequality with exponent [(1-alpha)(1+p(1-sigma))]/alpha>=0 and constant alpha^(-1-1/p). Right-endpoint indicators give the matching lower limit and strict interior weight proves no nonzero norm attainment at alpha<1. Left-endpoint indicators have explicitly computed norms in three cases p*sigma<1,=1,>1, yielding divergent ratios for alpha>1. Each boundary p=1, sigma=0/1, alpha=1 is covered; 422 supplementary assertions passed.

evidence: Raj et al. (2014), Theorem 1 and equation (5), assert a general measure-distortion norm formula; for x^alpha with alpha<1 it predicts 1/alpha, contradicted by the exact right-endpoint interval calculation alpha^(-1-1/p).

value.rationale: The exact sharp operator invariant for nonlinear power composition maps on the canonical Ces_p space and all intermediate primitive normalizations fills a mathematically motivated norm-computation gap where prior generic measure-distortion bounds are documented unreliable. One parameter-independent formula, an equality/nonattainment classification, and a sharp domain/composition phase boundary are obtained for all finite p. The two distinct endpoint indicator mechanisms explain stability and instability; this is neither a finite table nor an arbitrary tiny improvement.
